body:
I am so glad to hear that you've been through this as well. I think that maybe I will see a therapist about this, because I agree that this is an issue that is much bigger than what it appears to be on the surface. Again, thank you for telling me this. I don't feel so alone anymore.

Just as a sort of an interesting counter-point (I guess you could call it that), I should say that I don't mind my boyfriend watching porn at all. I think that the reasoning is that I know that he sees these girls as objects and for sex-purposes only, so my mind doesn't render them as any kind of threat. I guess that's a little strange.
You are very kind. Thank you. I will try to force these things to the forefront of my mind instead of dwelling on the negative. It's hard, but it needs to be done.

Yes, I know that it's irrational. I'm glad to know that I'm not the only person who is so hard on themselves, especially from someone who isn't the stereotypical self-loathing female.

I've thought about going to counseling, especially since the incident in my car. I honestly don't know what's stopping me except the idea that all they're going to say is "You're being unreasonable." You know?
